story.headline: Basel blow 2-0 lead at Thun
story.summary: Basel are winless in five league games after a 3-3 draw at Thun.
story.display_body: Basel have now gone five league games without a win, and SRF reports they still sit "below the line" in the table, one place behind Thun, who edged past Luzern with the point. Basel led 2–0 inside 12 minutes (Zan Celar after 40 seconds, Philip Otele), then goalkeeper Jonas Omlin tried to dribble on a slick pitch and handed Thun a goal; Kevin Rüegg's late own goal (78th minute) completed the comeback. Thun are still without a home league win after six attempts. SRF refers to Basel as the reigning champions, so five games without a win is a real slump. In the same round Lugano lost 5–0 at St. Gallen, while Servette–Zürich ended goalless. The league now pauses for two weeks of international matches; Basel host Luzern on Sunday 2026-11-22.
story.why: the Basel form that stalled at 0–0 against GC on 2026-10-25 has not recovered, and the international break gives the coach two weeks to fix a defence that gave away three goals to a side that had not won at home.

story.headline: Forest beat Man City 3-1
story.summary: Forest's 3-1 win ends City's dream start under Maresca.
story.display_body: BBC Sport frames the result as the end of City's "dream start" under Enzo Maresca, with the manager hearing "can we play you every week?" from the home crowd. Together with Brighton climbing to second (BBC Sport asks whether they are now Arsenal's main title challengers), the early table is looking less settled than the pre-season script suggested. Ten games is a small sample, so read this as a warning sign for City rather than a verdict.
story.why: a tight chasing pack means each dropped point by a leader carries more weight than usual this early.

story.headline: Norris wins Brazilian GP
story.summary: Norris won in the wet ahead of Verstappen as Mercedes clinched the constructors' title.
story.display_body: Lando Norris (McLaren) converted pole into his third win of 2026, holding off Max Verstappen, who finished second after starting from the back of the grid on an engine-change penalty; Isack Hadjar made it a double podium for Red Bull. Mercedes finished fourth and fifth (George Russell, new champion Kimi Antonelli) and that was enough to secure the constructors' championship, the team's ninth and first since 2021. The driver title was already decided, so the interest was in the team race and in Verstappen's recovery. Lewis Hamilton finished ninth and says tensions with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc are "squashed".
story.why: both titles now belong to Mercedes, so the remaining races are about pride, seats and 2027 positioning rather than the championship.

story.headline: Alcaraz wins Paris Masters
story.summary: Alcaraz beat Shelton 7-6, 7-5 for his first Paris title.
story.display_body: Carlos Alcaraz (ranked 3) beat Ben Shelton (ranked 4), saving a string of break points in the first set before winning a tiebreak, then breaking twice from behind in the second. SRF counts it as his seventh Masters 1000 title of the nine on the calendar; only the Canadian Open and Shanghai are missing. It follows his title in Vienna two weeks earlier and avenges Shelton's win over him in the US Open quarterfinals. Gauff opened the WTA Finals in Indian Wells with a three-set win over Pegula on 2026-11-09.
story.why: Alcaraz arrives at the season-ending finals in top form after a comeback from injury.

story.headline: Swiss hockey loses all three
story.summary: Switzerland lost all three Euro Hockey Tour games in Helsinki.
story.display_body: After losing 1–3 to Finland and 2–4 to Sweden, Switzerland led the Czechs 2–0 after the first period and still lost 2–4, finishing with zero points and a 5–11 goal difference. SRF notes the team has not won a game since its 6–0 win over Norway on 2026-05-30, and coach Jan Cadieux's squad is young. This is a preseason-style check-in, not a medal event, so one slump does not decide anything on its own.
story.why: a long winless run before the next major tournament is the kind of thing a young team needs to address early.

story.headline: Kremlin rules Europeans out of Abu Dhabi talks
story.summary: Kremlin says Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks on 10-11 November will be strictly trilateral, rejecting French statement that Europeans will be represented.
story.display_body: The Kremlin said on Monday 9 November that this week's Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, set for Tuesday 10 and Wednesday 11 November, will be strictly "trilateral" between Russia, Ukraine and the US, a day after France said Europeans would be represented. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said on Sunday 8 November that the E3 (France, Germany and the UK) would send their national security advisers, and that the European Commission would send Ursula von der Leyen's chief of staff, Björn Seibert. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov answered that the Americans and Ukrainians "have their own channels" to the Europeans. These are the first three-way talks since the US-Israeli war on Iran began on 28 February; an earlier Abu Dhabi round this year made no progress on territory. G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris on 9–10 November, partly so Europe can push for a seat at the table. Their worry is a CBS interview in which Donald Trump said Ukraine would "end up with a little bit different shape", meaning altered borders.
story.why: who sits in the room decides whether a deal over European security, and Ukraine's borders, is made without Europe.

story.headline: Qatar's premier carries Iran file to White House
story.summary: Trump hosts Qatar's PM on 9 November amid Qatari mediation of an Iranian proposal; Rubio sees no progress.
story.display_body: Donald Trump was due to host Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, at the White House on Monday 9 November, as Qatar carries messages between Washington and Tehran. On Thursday 5 November Iran sent a new nuclear and peace proposal through Qatari mediators. Tehran says it will only discuss the plan once the US accepts its seven preconditions, including sanctions relief, and the US says it is examining it. Trump said strikes are unlikely "if talks keep moving", but Secretary of State Marco Rubio says he sees no progress. On Sunday 8 November Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that Tehran would "rain down hell" if US attacks resume. The International Atomic Energy Agency (the UN nuclear watchdog) puts Iran's stock of uranium enriched to 60% at 440.9 kg; weapons-grade is about 90%.

story.headline: Trump calls deportations 'too tough', hires Miller
story.summary: Trump told CBS his deportation policy might be too tough for voters, then appointed Stephen Miller chief of staff.
story.display_body: In his first big interview since Republicans lost both houses of Congress in the midterms, Donald Trump told CBS on Sunday 8 November that his deportation policy "might be too tough" for voters and that an immigration deal with Democrats is "doable". He gave no details. Shortly after the interview he made Stephen Miller, the main architect of the hardline deportation drive, his chief of staff. That appointment points the opposite way from the softer words.
story.why: the new Congress will test whether any deal materialises. The White House's choice of staff is a better guide to policy than what Trump said on TV.

story.headline: COP31 opens in Antalya without the US
story.summary: UN climate summit COP31 opens in Antalya on 9 November with no US delegation; Turkey pushes 35-by-35 electrification pledge.
story.display_body: COP31, the annual UN climate summit, opened on Monday 9 November in Antalya, Turkey, with nearly 200 countries and over 100,000 participants expected over two weeks, and with no US delegation. The host is putting electrification at the centre with a non-binding "35 by 35" pledge: electricity should supply at least 35% of global energy demand by 2035, up from about a fifth today according to the International Energy Agency. The talks open against an energy-price crisis caused by the Iran war, a shortfall in climate-adaptation money, and forecasts that 2026 will be one of the four hottest years on record.
story.why: expectations are low. The test is whether earlier pledges turn into concrete, funded measures.

story.headline: Merz backs Aigner for German president
story.summary: Merz endorses CSU's Ilse Aigner to succeed Steinmeier as German federal president.
story.display_body: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Sunday 8 November that he backs Ilse Aigner of the Bavarian CSU, president of the Bavarian state parliament, as the next federal president, succeeding Frank-Walter Steinmeier early next year. The CDU leadership endorsed her on Sunday evening, and the party's federal executive and a joint press appearance were due on Monday 9 November. The SPD and Greens have already signalled support. If the Federal Convention (the body of MPs and state delegates that elects the president) confirms her, she would be Germany's first female head of state.

story.headline: Just Eat cuts 373 Swiss delivery jobs
story.summary: Just Eat confirms cutting 373 of about 700 Swiss jobs, moving to a flexible courier model unions call bogus self-employment.
story.display_body: Food-delivery company Just Eat confirmed on Monday 9 November that it is cutting 373 of its roughly 700 jobs in Switzerland: 193 directly employed couriers and 180 agency workers in Zurich, Winterthur, Bern, Biel, Fribourg and St. Gallen. The company says its shift-based model is no longer competitive and it will move to a "more flexible" delivery model. Talks on a social plan are still under way. The unions Unia and Syndicom call the new model bogus self-employment that avoids labour and social-insurance law. They point to the Zurich social-insurance office (SVA), which said last week that platforms cannot choose their workers' status themselves. The unions want the cantons and the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) to step in.
story.why: this follows SRF's late-October report on Uber Eats pushing local bike couriers out of the market. Whether authorities enforce employee status will decide what delivery work in Switzerland looks like.

story.headline: 38% of apprentices reach tertiary degree
story.summary: FSO: 38% of 2012 CFC holders obtained a tertiary qualification within 12 years, strongly dependent on parental education.
story.display_body: Thirty-eight percent of people who earned a federal apprenticeship certificate (CFC/EFZ) in 2012 had a tertiary qualification 12 years later, the Federal Statistical Office reported on Monday 9 November. The most common routes were a federal professional diploma (15%), a higher vocational college (12%) and a bachelor's from a university of applied sciences or a university of teacher education (9%). Rates ranged from 59% in nursing to 23% in retail and personal services, and from 30% at micro-firms to 43% at large firms. Family background mattered most: the rate was over 50% when a parent had a tertiary degree, and 27% when neither parent had finished upper-secondary school.
story.why: it puts a number on how open the apprenticeship-to-higher-education route really is, and on how much it still depends on parents.

story.headline: Vaud overhauls its tax administration
story.summary: Vaud reorganises its tax administration by 2028 after a BDO governance audit ordered over the bouclier fiscal affair.
story.display_body: Vaud's finance department announced on Monday 9 November that it will reorganise the canton's tax administration (DGF) by 2028, based on a governance audit by BDO that was published the same day. The audit was ordered in August 2025 after the controversy over how the canton applied its "bouclier fiscal" (a tax cap). It found the DGF does its job as required, but recommended a phased overhaul of strategy, governance, processes and communication. This is the first step in a programme running to 2032 that is meant to prepare the canton for major tax reforms.
